basis: Acquired proximal tubular dysfunction causes renal solute wasting, including phosphate depletion and bicarbonate loss.
Toxic injury and inflammation of the bronchioles; no infectious or immune-mediated mechanism established.
Epileptic encephalopathy with severe developmental impairment; apnea does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Central motor disorder with spastic quadriplegia and cerebral abnormalities; no established additional organ damage.
Spinal vascular malformation and chronic venous congestion cause necrotizing spinal cord injury.
Central and peripheral neurodegeneration; gait impairment and hypotonia do not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Storage causes splenic/marrow disease and hepatic infiltration in 80–99%; skeletal damage in 30–79%. Neurologic disease is subtype-dependent and omitted under the cap.
Localized middle-ear cholesterol granuloma with a chronic foreign-body inflammatory response.
Contact lens-associated corneal edema is confined to the eye.
Infantile interstitial lung disease; glycogen-containing interstitial cells do not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis with anemia and abnormal erythrocyte morphology.
Maternal anti-Kell antibodies destroy fetal erythrocytes and suppress erythropoiesis; alloimmune blood disease.
Structural congenital myopathy with muscle weakness and hand atrophy; facial weakness and hyporeflexia can be myopathic.
Hypothalamic hamartoma with seizures and characteristic endocrine dysfunction; skeletal malformations include polydactyly in 2/2 annotated patients.
Ovarian endocrine failure: hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and absent puberty in 5/5; therefore an endocrine axis applies.
Perinatal gas-exchange failure; supplied synonyms explicitly include neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Other organ injury varies with severity.
Primary hepatic embryonal tumor; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish another affected organ.
Intellectual developmental disorder classified as ST3GAL3 congenital disorder of glycosylation, an inherited metabolic defect.
Melanoma occupying the esophageal wall; the concept does not establish a cutaneous primary site.
EBV-driven epithelial hyperplasia of oral mucosa; associated HIV is a separate condition.
Congenital facial nerve dysfunction; hearing impairment is variable, with no frequency establishing involvement in at least 30%.
Glutathione synthesis defect with hemolysis; intellectual disability in 2/4 supports neurologic involvement. HPO findings conflict with the restricted subtype name.
Myopathy with defining cardiomyopathy; demyelinating neuropathy in 1/3. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle/diaphragm weakness, without intrinsic lung damage.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; optic atrophy in 1/2 supports ocular damage. Feeding difficulty and constipation do not establish direct gut damage.
Umbrella hereditary spastic ataxia affecting central motor and cerebellar pathways; extra-neurologic findings are subtype-specific.
